newsitem.title: PHILIPPINES: Philippine peso gains at close from inflows.
newsitem.headline: Philippine peso gains at close from inflows.

text.p: *Central Bank says peso strengthened by investor money
The Philippine peso continued to gain on Wednesday amid the steady inflows of dollars for direct and portfolio investments, traders said.
It closed at 26.298 against the dollar from 26.306, with the day's average at 26.302 from 26.315. Volume was lower at $116.80 million from $190.50 million.
The Central Bank said the peso, although weakened last week by speculation, was being strengthened by large capital inflows.
The peso hit a 27-month low of 26.345 last week after a sell-off by speculators due to a sharp fall in domestic interest rates triggered by a reserve requirement cut.
"Such overreaction was negated by strong investor confidence in the Philippines," Central Bank Governor Gabriel Singson said.
But a trader said "the market's still a little cautious. The Central Bank should not let interest rates go lower."
Traders said the Central Bank had not yet intervened in the market to curb the peso's strength.
"It (the Central Bank) doesn't want to rack the market. Banks may buy dollars again," another dealer said.
But the Central Bank quoted lower bid and offer rates for the dollar at 26.255 and 26.305 respectively from an earlier 26.27/26.32, traders said.
Looking ahead, the peso is likely to continue its trek upwards but it could be capped at 26.28 by the Central Bank, a trader predicted.
